title: Diversity, Prejudice and Discrimination
summary: Diversity in South Africa, stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination, forms of discrimination such as racism, sexism and xenophobia, and how to promote inclusion and nation-building.

notes.text: **Diversity** means differences between people: culture, language, race, religion, gender, age, ability, nationality and beliefs. South Africa has **12 official languages** (including South African Sign Language since 2023) and many cultures and religions. Our motto, *!ke e: ǀxarra ǁke*, means **'diverse people unite'**.

rows: A fixed, oversimplified **idea** about a group of people
A negative **attitude or feeling** towards someone because of the group they belong to, formed without knowing them
Disliking someone because of their accent
Unfair **action or treatment** because of a person's group
Refusing to pick someone for a team because of their nationality

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Stereotypes are **thoughts**, prejudice is a **feeling**, and discrimination is an **action**. Each can lead to the next.

rows: Being from another country (fear or hatred of foreigners)

notes.text: Section 9 of the Constitution forbids **unfair discrimination** on grounds including race, gender, sex, pregnancy, marital status, ethnic or social origin, colour, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, conscience, belief, culture, language and birth.

items: Victims feel hurt, excluded, angry and may develop low self-esteem or depression.
Communities become divided; distrust and conflict grow.
Talent is wasted when people are denied opportunities.
It can lead to violence, such as xenophobic attacks.
**Learn** about other cultures, languages and religions; ask respectful questions.
**Challenge** stereotypes and jokes that put others down.
Celebrate days such as **Heritage Day** (24 September), **Human Rights Day** (21 March) and **Freedom Day** (27 April).
Practise **ubuntu**: 'I am because we are' (*umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu*), the idea that we are connected and should treat each other with compassion.

notes.label: Nation-building
notes.text: Nation-building means working together to create a united, fair society that respects diversity. Sport, music and national symbols (the flag, anthem and coat of arms) help bring people together.
